results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

### The second increase this year

This is not the first increase. The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10. [2] Our own catalog recorded H100 at $3.85 on September 18 and B300 at $7.85 on September 24.

If the May figures are right, the October rates are about 53% higher for H100 and 56% higher for B300 than five months earlier. [2] The trend matters more than any single rate. A budget built on spring pricing may already be out of date.

...

Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

### What to do before October 1

Ask about locking today's rate. Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate. Get the answer in writing, with the rate and term.

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

If you are planning a project, get a dated quote for your actual start date. Ask what a 3, 6 or 12 month commitment costs against the new on demand rate. Ask whether that commitment reserves GPUs or only lowers the rate.

results.title: Nebius raises on-demand GPU prices from 1 October | VETTDD
results.author: Editor Editorial desk, VETTDD
highlights:
The neocloud’s published price list lifts H100, H200, B200 and B300 hourly rates by 17–21%, and partners reselling AI compute are likely to need to rebase their quotes

...

The facts

- Spot prices for preemptible HGX H100 and H200 instances start from $0.79 (£0.60) per GPU-hour, and Nebius says they can change as often as every 15 minutes.
- Nebius’s pricing FAQ gives US dollars as the only currency it accepts.
- Egress and ingress traffic, public IP addresses and Nebius’s managed Kubernetes service are listed as free.

Why it matters

Buyers renting GPU capacity on demand should assume that neocloud prices can rise mid-project and budget with headroom. Where workloads are steady, reserved capacity is now the main way to hold costs, so compare a committed term against the hyperscalers before renewing. UK buyers also carry currency risk on dollar-only billing. Check contracts for how much notice a supplier must give before a rate change and whether in-flight work is protected.

Nebius will charge more for on-demand graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity from 1 October 2026, according to the price list on its website. An Nvidia HGX H100 instance rises from $3.85 (£2.91) to $4.50 (£3.40) per GPU-hour, and an HGX B300 from $7.85 (£5.93) to $9.50 (£7.17).

The rest of the HGX range moves the same way. H200 goes from $4.50 to $5.40 (£4.08) and B200 from $7.15 (£5.40) to $8.50 (£6.42). On the page’s own figures, the four rises run from 17% to 21%. Central processing unit (CPU) instances go up too, with AMD Epyc Genoa starting at $0.13 (£0.10) an hour instead of $0.10. RTX Pro 6000 and L40S prices are unchanged, and the rack-scale GB300 and GB200 NVL72 systems remain price on request.

Silicon UK, which reported the change on 18 September, said it is the company’s second rise in three months, taking B300 pricing up a cumulative 56%, and that memory offerings will rise by 41%. Silicon UK also reported that CoreWeave had said the same day that it was signing new contracts at higher prices. The Nebius page still offers up to 35% off on-demand rates for large clusters reserved for several months.

results.title: Nebius will raise hourly GPU prices by up to 21% on Oct. 1 · Infive
highlights:
Nebius will raise on-demand rates for four Nvidia GPU models by 17% to 21% on Oct. 1, including B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 an hour. CFO Dado Alonso said in August that capacity sold out as fast as it came online; existing contracts won't be repriced.

The increases cover H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPUs, plus CPU-only servers. Nebius listed the H100 at $2.95 an hour and the B300 at $6.10 in early May; after the new rates, they will cost $4.50 and $9.50—about 53% and 56% more, respectively.

Nebius does not disclose how much revenue comes from hourly rentals versus reserved-capacity contracts. At June's end, it reported $37.5 billion in remaining performance obligations—signed revenue not yet recognized—more than 60 times its $582 million second-quarter revenue. The Oct. 1 increase won't reprice that backlog and mainly signals rates for capacity not yet sold; the article warns prices could fall if supply catches up.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

This price adjustment sends a significant signal: the pace of growth in AI computing demand may still outstrip the rate at which high-end GPUs, power, and data center capacity are coming online. Unlike traditional cloud computing, the core scarce resources for AI cloud services extend beyond servers to include GPU availability, power access, liquid cooling systems, networking equipment, and data centers capable of supporting high-density racks. If any single component encounters a bottleneck, new computing power cannot be rapidly deployed.

At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Nebius management stated that the company's visibility into customer demand has extended from approximately 18 months to over 24 months, with some customers already reserving compute capacity for the first half of 2028. The company previously conducted price testing for scarce Blackwell capacity, achieving transaction prices approximately 15% higher than previous peak prices and roughly 20% higher than standard sales pipeline quotes.

The significance of Nebius's price increase lies not merely in the ability to charge approximately 20% more per GPU hour, but in confirming that supply and demand in the AI computing market still favor suppliers. A primary past market concern was that simultaneous launches of numerous data centers could eventually lead to GPU leasing market oversupply, potentially resulting in lower utilization rates, extended payback periods, and asset impairment for companies built under assumptions of higher prices. Nebius signals the opposite: the company is raising prices not only for new B200 and B300 models but also for H100 and H200, which have been on the market for years. This indicates that demand extends beyond the latest architecture, with previous-generation GPUs still offering sufficient performance and cost efficiency for model fine-tuning, inference, scientific computing, and certain enterprise workloads.

...

However, the on-demand price increase will not uniformly raise all of Nebius's revenue by 20%. Large customers typically sign multi-year contracts with fixed prices, minimum purchase volumes, and service terms that cannot be immediately repriced according to new public rates. This adjustment most directly impacts on-demand and short-term compute contracts rather than long-term capacity agreements already signed by clients like Meta.

results.title: Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now. | Devanshu Rajput
results.author: Devanshu Rajput
highlights:
Nebius just confirmed the price increase we flagged as unconfirmed last week. Its live now.

H100 pricing on Nebius went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, confirmed directly against their own pricing page, a 17% increase. H200 rose 20%, from $4.50 to $5.40. B300 climbed 21%, reaching $9.50. This is Nebius's second rate hike since May, when H100 was still priced at $2.95.

According to GetDeploying's pricing tracker, the median on-demand H100 across 40 providers sat at $3.42/GPU-hour as of September 28, up 15% year over year. The same tracker puts hyperscaler pricing at roughly 58% above specialized GPU clouds for the same chip.

Nobody builds a futures market for a commodity that's reliably getting cheaper. CME Group is launching GPU rental price futures on October 5. That alone signals where this market expects prices to go next.

results.title: Amazon is hiking chip-rental prices and reportedly moving Nvidia processors off the balance sheet
highlights:
In a sign of the financing crunch facing the hyperscalers backing the AI revolution, Amazon has announced it is raising prices on how much it charges to rent high-performance microchips as it reportedly is going to sell and then lease back Nvidia chips.

Amazon AMZN on Friday said it is raising prices, by about 15%, starting next week, for what’s called EC2 Capacity Blocks, which provide access to computing power on Nvidia chips ranging from the older A100 to the newer, more high-performance B300.
